rep-hal: Haleakalā summit: Lynch could not convince himself he saw any curvature.
rep-mk: Mauna Kea summit: the same — no curvature he could be sure of.
rep-jet: Airliner, clear horizon: “subtle but unmistakable” across a field of 90° or more, not discernible under about 60°; most airline pilots say they cannot see it.
rep-b57: B-57 (D. Gutierrez): the curvature “does not become readily sensible until about 50,000 ft”.
rep-pic: Piccard and Kipfer's balloon, 1931: the first sighting of the curvature, as widely attributed.
rep-b60: 60,000 ft: “obvious” (Gutierrez); Concorde passengers “routinely marveled” at it.
rep-exp: Explorer II balloon, 1935: the first photographs of the curvature.
